formation.explanation: A client command enters the leader's applyCh (B-apply-api) and is dispatched by the leader main loop (B-leader-dispatch), which assigns (Index,Term), stores it in the local LogStore, marks its own matchIndex and notifies replicators. Followers accept entries through AppendEntries only after the PrevLog identity matches and truncate conflicting suffixes (B-follower-append). Whenever any server reports that it has stored up to an index, commitment.match/recalculate raises commitIndex to the quorum median once it is at or beyond the leader's startIndex (B-quorum-commit, B-commit-term-rule). The leader then applies committed entries in index order to the FSM and resolves client futures (B-leader-apply).

context.explanation: Authority is a per-term value. Each node persists its current term and any vote through StableStore before acting (B-term-vote-persist). A follower whose heartbeat timer expires starts a candidate campaign, soliciting votes or pre-votes from voters of the latest configuration and winning at quorumSize (B-election); the winner's leadership is the context in which log dispatch is legal. Context is lost whenever a higher term is observed in any RPC or replication response (B-authority-loss) or when the leader fails its lease check (B-leader-lease); both transitions clear the known leader and invalidate the previous term's leadership.

connection.explanation: The two core lines meet at the startIndex rule and at the voter set. A leader may only advance commitIndex once a quorum of the current configuration has stored the first entry of the leader's term (B-commit-term-rule over B-quorum-commit), so formation is gated by current-term authority. Conversely, authority is defined over the voter configuration (B-election, B-config-eligibility), and losing authority (B-authority-loss) aborts pending formation work: runLeader's deferred cleanup answers inflight futures with ErrLeadershipLost while the durable log prefix and the already-applied FSM state remain. Established decisions from earlier terms persist as log entries but cannot be committed by a new leader until its own term entry is quorum-matched.

selections.rationale: First Candidate on the accepted v1 map, selected from the A1/A2 connection. The commit index is advanced by the commitment object (F-committed, established by B-quorum-commit/B-commit-term-rule) while client futures are completed by the leader main goroutine's inflight handling (B-leader-apply). The two are linked only through a capacity-1 commitCh and runLeader's deferred cleanup, so the ordering at an authority transition is not evident from the data structures alone. This question isolates whether every index counted as committed is consumed (applied in order, or later delivered from the durable log) and whether a future can be answered ErrLeadershipLost for an entry already counted committed. It is a lifecycle/consumption question for one principal Fact with a sourced A1 relationship and A2 context support; no violation is presumed.

Source reading answers this Candidate's specific suspicion, so the question is disposed as explained by existing mechanisms rather than escalated. The leaderLoop commitCh case reads commitment.getCommitIndex(), calls setCommitIndex and runs processLogs synchronously on the same goroutine, so a consumed notification cannot skip or reorder entries; if a higher-term RPC is selected before the notification is consumed, runLeader's deferred cleanup answers the still-inflight futures with ErrLeadershipLost and the entries remain durable. formation.explanation: A client command enters the leader's applyCh (B-apply-api) and is dispatched by the leader main loop (B-leader-dispatch), which assigns (Index,Term), stores it in the local LogStore, marks its own matchIndex and notifies replicators. Followers accept entries through AppendEntries only after the PrevLog identity matches and truncate conflicting suffixes (B-follower-append). Whenever any server reports that it has stored up to an index, commitment.match/recalculate raises commitIndex to the quorum median once it is at or beyond the leader's startIndex (B-quorum-commit, B-commit-term-rule). The leader then applies committed entries in index order to the FSM and resolves client futures (B-leader-apply).

context.explanation: Authority is a per-term value. Each node persists its current term and any vote through StableStore before acting (B-term-vote-persist). A follower whose heartbeat timer expires starts a candidate campaign, soliciting votes or pre-votes from voters of the latest configuration and winning at quorumSize (B-election); the winner's leadership is the context in which log dispatch is legal. Context is lost whenever a higher term is observed in any RPC or replication response (B-authority-loss) or when the leader fails its lease check (B-leader-lease); both transitions clear the known leader and invalidate the previous term's leadership.

connection.explanation: The two core lines meet at the startIndex rule and at the voter set. A leader may only advance commitIndex once a quorum of the current configuration has stored the first entry of the leader's term (B-commit-term-rule over B-quorum-commit), so formation is gated by current-term authority. Conversely, authority is defined over the voter configuration (B-election, B-config-eligibility), and losing authority (B-authority-loss) aborts pending formation work: runLeader's deferred cleanup answers inflight futures with ErrLeadershipLost while the durable log prefix and the already-applied FSM state remain. Established decisions from earlier terms persist as log entries but cannot be committed by a new leader until its own term entry is quorum-matched.

formation.explanation: A client command enters the leader's applyCh (B-apply-api) and is dispatched by the leader main loop (B-leader-dispatch), which assigns (Index,Term), stores it in the local LogStore, marks its own matchIndex and notifies replicators. Followers accept entries through AppendEntries only after the PrevLog identity matches and truncate conflicting suffixes (B-follower-append). Whenever any server reports that it has stored up to an index, commitment.match/recalculate raises commitIndex to the quorum median once it is at or beyond the leader's startIndex (B-quorum-commit, B-commit-term-rule). The leader then applies committed entries in index order to the FSM and resolves client futures (B-leader-apply).

context.explanation: Authority is a per-term value. Each node persists its current term and any vote through StableStore before acting (B-term-vote-persist). A follower whose heartbeat timer expires starts a candidate campaign, soliciting votes or pre-votes from voters of the latest configuration and winning at quorumSize (B-election); the winner's leadership is the context in which log dispatch is legal. Context is lost whenever a higher term is observed in any RPC or replication response (B-authority-loss) or when the leader fails its lease check (B-leader-lease); both transitions clear the known leader and invalidate the previous term's leadership.

connection.explanation: The two core lines meet at the startIndex rule and at the voter set. A leader may only advance commitIndex once a quorum of the current configuration has stored the first entry of the leader's term (B-commit-term-rule over B-quorum-commit), so formation is gated by current-term authority. Conversely, authority is defined over the voter configuration (B-election, B-config-eligibility), and losing authority (B-authority-loss) aborts pending formation work: runLeader's deferred cleanup answers inflight futures with ErrLeadershipLost while the durable log prefix and the already-applied FSM state remain. Established decisions from earlier terms persist as log entries but cannot be committed by a new leader until its own term entry is quorum-matched.

The transport decodes each command, classifies strictly entry-less AppendEntries as heartbeats, and either calls the registered heartbeat handler directly on the connection goroutine or dispatches the RPC to the main consumer. The NewRaft comment requires that fast path to be safe when called concurrently with a blocking RPC, so the question is what the fast-path handler actually touches; reading it shows only atomic state writes, the leader lock and the last-contact lock, which is what makes the concurrent call safe. feedback.answered: The heartbeat fast path is safe as documented, and the transport's RPC admission adds no separate obligation. In the transport, each command is decoded, an InstallSnapshot reader is bounded by io.LimitReader(r, req.Size), and an AppendEntries command is treated as a heartbeat only under a strict conjunction - non-zero term, a leader address, PrevLogEntry and PrevLogTerm zero, no entries and LeaderCommitIndex zero - so an entry-carrying or commit-carrying AppendEntries always goes to the main consumer. When the fast path applies and a handler is registered, the handler is invoked directly on the connection goroutine; reading processHeartbeat and the appendEntries path it reaches shows that for such an entry-less heartbeat the handler can only call setState/setCurrentTerm (atomic stores), setLeader (which takes leaderLock and publishes an observation only on change), the previous-log check (skipped because PrevLogEntry is zero), the entries block (skipped because there are no entries), the commit update (skipped because LeaderCommitIndex is zero) and setLastContact (lastContactLock), and it reads the cached last index for the response under the state lock. No plain configurations field is written and no LogStore call is made on that path, so calling it concurrently with a blocking RPC does not race the main loop's configuration or storage mutations. The heartbeat classification is therefore load-bearing: it is what keeps the fast path free of the state the main thread owns.

feedback.answered: The ordering defect has two sourced consequences at startup, and they are consequences of the confirmed defect rather than separate obligations. The lower-index choice is what enables both outcomes: with the contract-conformant ordering the higher snapshot index would cover the hole.

feedback.answered: The vote-withholding scenario is identified and ready to construct, using the same premise as the first confirmed append scenario. After a follower truncates its conflicting suffix and the following StoreLogs fails, its real log ends at the surviving prefix (index 1, term 1) while its cached last entry still reads (index 3, term 2). The check's discriminator is therefore the handler's own Granted field: granted should be true and is expected false. This would move the claim's consequence from append rejection to vote withholding, which is the availability question the claim's unknowns leave open, and it needs the same injectable failing store and the same conflict drive as the accepted first scenario, plus a direct requestVote call on the same node.

formation.explanation: A client command enters the leader's applyCh (B-apply-api) and is dispatched by the leader main loop (B-leader-dispatch), which assigns (Index,Term), stores it in the local LogStore, marks its own matchIndex and notifies replicators. Followers accept entries through AppendEntries only after the PrevLog identity matches and truncate conflicting suffixes (B-follower-append). Whenever any server reports that it has stored up to an index, commitment.match/recalculate raises commitIndex to the quorum median once it is at or beyond the leader's startIndex (B-quorum-commit, B-commit-term-rule). The leader then applies committed entries in index order to the FSM and resolves client futures (B-leader-apply).

context.explanation: Authority is a per-term value. Each node persists its current term and any vote through StableStore before acting (B-term-vote-persist). A follower whose heartbeat timer expires starts a candidate campaign, soliciting votes or pre-votes from voters of the latest configuration and winning at quorumSize (B-election); the winner's leadership is the context in which log dispatch is legal. Context is lost whenever a higher term is observed in any RPC or replication response (B-authority-loss) or when the leader fails its lease check (B-leader-lease); both transitions clear the known leader and invalidate the previous term's leadership.

connection.explanation: The two core lines meet at the startIndex rule and at the voter set. A leader may only advance commitIndex once a quorum of the current configuration has stored the first entry of the leader's term (B-commit-term-rule over B-quorum-commit), so formation is gated by current-term authority. Conversely, authority is defined over the voter configuration (B-election, B-config-eligibility), and losing authority (B-authority-loss) aborts pending formation work: runLeader's deferred cleanup answers inflight futures with ErrLeadershipLost while the durable log prefix and the already-applied FSM state remain. Established decisions from earlier terms persist as log entries but cannot be committed by a new leader until its own term entry is quorum-matched.

selections.rationale: First Candidate on the accepted v1 map, selected from the A1/A2 connection. The commit index is advanced by the commitment object (F-committed, established by B-quorum-commit/B-commit-term-rule) while client futures are completed by the leader main goroutine's inflight handling (B-leader-apply). The two are linked only through a capacity-1 commitCh and runLeader's deferred cleanup, so the ordering at an authority transition is not evident from the data structures alone. This question isolates whether every index counted as committed is consumed (applied in order, or later delivered from the durable log) and whether a future can be answered ErrLeadershipLost for an entry already counted committed. It is a lifecycle/consumption question for one principal Fact with a sourced A1 relationship and A2 context support; no violation is presumed.

Source reading answers this Candidate's specific suspicion, so the question is disposed as explained by existing mechanisms rather than escalated. The leaderLoop commitCh case reads commitment.getCommitIndex(), calls setCommitIndex and runs processLogs synchronously on the same goroutine, so a consumed notification cannot skip or reorder entries; if a higher-term RPC is selected before the notification is consumed, runLeader's deferred cleanup answers the still-inflight futures with ErrLeadershipLost and the entries remain durable. The public Apply contract explicitly documents that case as indeterminate ('There is no way to guarantee whether the write succeeded or failed'), and the node applies the committed index later from its durable log via the new leader's LeaderCommitIndex. No violation is presumed and no map change is proposed; the previously recorded edges and Behaviors still apply.

feedback.answered: Every index counted as committed by commitment.recalculate is either applied in order (processLogs walks idx from lastApplied+1 to index, taking each entry from the inflight futures map or the LogStore, and only then sets lastApplied) or, if the leader steps down before the commitCh notification is consumed, remains in the durable log and is applied on this node later when a leader supplies LeaderCommitIndex (follower appendEntries -> setCommitIndex(min(LeaderCommitIndex,lastIndex)) -> processLogs(idx,nil)). formation.explanation: A client command enters the leader's applyCh (B-apply-api) and is dispatched by the leader main loop (B-leader-dispatch), which assigns (Index,Term), stores it in the local LogStore, marks its own matchIndex and notifies replicators. Followers accept entries through AppendEntries only after the PrevLog identity matches and truncate conflicting suffixes (B-follower-append). Whenever any server reports that it has stored up to an index, commitment.match/recalculate raises commitIndex to the quorum median once it is at or beyond the leader's startIndex (B-quorum-commit, B-commit-term-rule). The leader then applies committed entries in index order to the FSM and resolves client futures (B-leader-apply).

context.explanation: Authority is a per-term value. Each node persists its current term and any vote through StableStore before acting (B-term-vote-persist). A follower whose heartbeat timer expires starts a candidate campaign, soliciting votes or pre-votes from voters of the latest configuration and winning at quorumSize (B-election); the winner's leadership is the context in which log dispatch is legal. Context is lost whenever a higher term is observed in any RPC or replication response (B-authority-loss) or when the leader fails its lease check (B-leader-lease); both transitions clear the known leader and invalidate the previous term's leadership.

connection.explanation: The two core lines meet at the startIndex rule and at the voter set. A leader may only advance commitIndex once a quorum of the current configuration has stored the first entry of the leader's term (B-commit-term-rule over B-quorum-commit), so formation is gated by current-term authority. Conversely, authority is defined over the voter configuration (B-election, B-config-eligibility), and losing authority (B-authority-loss) aborts pending formation work: runLeader's deferred cleanup answers inflight futures with ErrLeadershipLost while the durable log prefix and the already-applied FSM state remain. Established decisions from earlier terms persist as log entries but cannot be committed by a new leader until its own term entry is quorum-matched.

formation.explanation: A client command enters the leader's applyCh (B-apply-api) and is dispatched by the leader main loop (B-leader-dispatch), which assigns (Index,Term), stores it in the local LogStore, marks its own matchIndex and notifies replicators. Followers accept entries through AppendEntries only after the PrevLog identity matches and truncate conflicting suffixes (B-follower-append). Whenever any server reports that it has stored up to an index, commitment.match/recalculate raises commitIndex to the quorum median once it is at or beyond the leader's startIndex (B-quorum-commit, B-commit-term-rule). The leader then applies committed entries in index order to the FSM and resolves client futures (B-leader-apply).

context.explanation: Authority is a per-term value. Each node persists its current term and any vote through StableStore before acting (B-term-vote-persist). A follower whose heartbeat timer expires starts a candidate campaign, soliciting votes or pre-votes from voters of the latest configuration and winning at quorumSize (B-election); the winner's leadership is the context in which log dispatch is legal. Context is lost whenever a higher term is observed in any RPC or replication response (B-authority-loss) or when the leader fails its lease check (B-leader-lease); both transitions clear the known leader and invalidate the previous term's leadership.

connection.explanation: The two core lines meet at the startIndex rule and at the voter set. A leader may only advance commitIndex once a quorum of the current configuration has stored the first entry of the leader's term (B-commit-term-rule over B-quorum-commit), so formation is gated by current-term authority. Conversely, authority is defined over the voter configuration (B-election, B-config-eligibility), and losing authority (B-authority-loss) aborts pending formation work: runLeader's deferred cleanup answers inflight futures with ErrLeadershipLost while the durable log prefix and the already-applied FSM state remain. Established decisions from earlier terms persist as log entries but cannot be committed by a new leader until its own term entry is quorum-matched.

feedback.answered: A client future created by Apply/ApplyLog does not receive the node's shutdown channel, so its Error() method can block forever rather than returning when the node stops. In the shared deferError, Error() selects only on the response channel or on d.ShutdownCh, and init() creates only the response channel; the three places that set ShutdownCh on a future are the user-restore future, the snapshot-install future and the snapshot request, so a logFuture from Apply has a nil ShutdownCh. The main run loop exits when shutdownCh closes without draining applyCh, and Shutdown closes shutdownCh and sets the state without responding to futures already enqueued. With the default unbuffered applyCh a send only succeeds when the loop receives the future, but Config.BatchApplyCh buffers the channel, so a future can be accepted while the loop is busy and then be abandoned when the node shuts down, leaving the caller blocked in Error() indefinitely.
remaining: Whether an Apply future can actually be pending at shutdown with BatchApplyCh enabled, which needs a running loop and a controlled schedule to observe.
